headline: An Italian prankster fooled professors and a Nobel laureate with a fake Umberto Eco column on AI that he made with ChatGPT in half an hour.
score_reason: Widely shared hoax exposed by several fact-checkers and admitted by its author; the posting was 1 Oct, the exposure within the window.
importance_line: Readers learn that a convincing fake essay by a famous author now takes one person and half an hour, and that intellectuals share first and check later; the only doubt is how far beyond Italy the page travelled.
summary: Finestre sull'Arte reports that a fake 2010 L'Espresso column by the late semiotician Umberto Eco, titled "The Machine That Will Have Read Everything" and hailed as his prophecy of ChatGPT, was exposed by fact-checkers Open, BUTAC and Tlon after Nobel physicist Giorgio Parisi and other scholars shared it; its author, veteran online prankster Ciro Ascione, then admitted he posted it on 1 Oct 2026 and built it "in half an hour using ChatGPT". The giveaways were an image-generator artifact in the page and a date that fell on a Sunday, when the magazine is not sold.
notes: Hoax posted 1 Oct; the debunking and author's admission are the new part. Machine-translated article.
